title: Expert versus data-learned fuzzy rules for cognitive-offloading risk in student–LLM dialogues: code, analysis plans and manuscript build
description: Code for the manuscript 'Expert versus Data-Learned Fuzzy Rules for Cognitive-Offloading Risk in Student–LLM Tutoring Dialogues: A Cross-Semester Evaluation' (submitted to Applied Soft Computing). Includes weak-label and feature construction for the StudyChat corpus; an expert five-rule TSK rule base with Łukasiewicz implication constraints (E1–E6); outcome-checked rules (E7–E9); a count-based TSK rule base with learned consequents (CF-TSK) evaluated across semesters (E10), with input selection nested in the training semester (E11) and with an LSTM encoder (E12); the in-archive benchmark, ablation, permutation and complementarity analyses; the analysis plans PREREG_E7_E9/E10/E11/E12.md committed before each run (see git-history.bundle); a frozen CF-TSK model trained on Fall 2024; and a renderer that builds the manuscript from the statistics file. StudyChat data are not included (access-gated, CC BY 4.0).
